describe: Primitive 3D reproduction: asymmetric tank, facing-marked infantry, raised ground patch and box prop; pan/orbit/zoom, pick and reset.
Authoritative terrain and obstacles: ridge, slope threshold, forest volume, road, water with bridge, low/tall/thin walls; click probes the exported surface; overlay toggles.
One authority in a worker: real tick commands with an ordered ack log, pause/step/reset, withheld consumer credit and an in-thread replay/parity check.

Routing and group intent: shortest vs fastest routes, group destinations, friendly traffic, a wall injected at tick 150, route-blocked destinations; select/drag, right-click, double right-click, Shift queue, S stop.

Own sensors and shared identification: a scripted red tank tours thin forest, deep forest, the ridge's far side and a building's shadow; ground fog; per-unit own-sensor lists; labelled side-view switch.

Physical flight and swept collision: gravity arcs, a fast bullet leading a thin sliding target, dodge after launch, a hill crest blocking direct fire while the indirect high arc clears it, and bodies crossing a round's line between ticks.
Uncertain evidence: a hidden squad fires every 3 s (stable firing area), a tank leaves a fixed last-seen area when it drives behind the hill, synthesized sound cues with captions.

Independent weapons: a rifle squad (rifles + grenade launcher) and a tank (cannon with AP/HE + HMG) against a red tank that ducks behind a wall and a hidden squad firing from behind a building; per-mount aim/reload bars and action reasons; attack identified/contact/ground, attack-move, engagement policy switch.

Consequences of physical fire: HE into an exposed squad and a forest squad side by side, a friendly squad close enough to share the blast, a red tank destroyed in a walled passage whose wreck reroutes a supply truck, fallen soldiers that stay, and suppression halos.

Reversible deployment: a supply truck sets up where it stands; deploy, pack, Stop and (queued) moves reverse one progress value with equal durations both ways; a ground ring and the panel show progress and the end state it heads to, and the folded pose follows progress.

Supported AT guidance: an AT team launches only on its own sight (a scout's is not enough), guides one missile at a time, and releases it at once on moving, Stop or losing sight; the released missile flies on to its fixed last point. Variants: late escape, prompt escape, prepared crossfire.

Buildings as fighting positions: two blue squads share a building by soldier capacity (a third is refused), enter and leave on a timer, and fire outward from perimeter slots while red's rounds hit occupants or the walls; a red squad behind the building is seen only once occupants stand on that facade; red's tank brings the building down into a lower, impassable ruin and survivors escape pinned.

Recovery with finite stock: a supply truck sets up (15 s) and serves a damaged tank, an AT team short of missiles and a rifle squad with casualties; moving units wait; stock falls and never regrows; an empty truck leaves its neighbours waiting for stock; relocation.

The ground layer: two tanks race east, one through an authored crater field (craters slow vehicles slightly, never their plan); two tanks shell a red squad in craters and one in the open; a squad walks the field; a flat cell debug view of the authoritative craters, scorch, tracks and trampling.

Weapon readouts: world-anchored aim and reload rings per weapon with rounds left (∞ unlimited), guidance icon and a separate deployment square; the selected-unit panel keeps every detail when zoomed out; the command bar exposes every village action (A attack-move, G attack ground, S stop, E fire policy).
The village encounter: blue attacks the defended village (red defender policy on its own observation), with the production readouts, command bar, variant and seed, pause/reset, and replay export.

The scripted benchmark (the one frame-cost measure): the village warm-started to heavy contact with blue on the supported script, a keyframed camera tour through strategic, pan, zoom, ground, combined and return, then the results screen and JSON report. The scene runs the 60 s short run and writes the frame-cost row.
Village replay: load a saved battle; the defender and input are off, the accepted commands of both sides replay, and a mismatched fixture is refused with a clear error.

Synthetic stress battle for the scale verdict (slice 16): 100 units a side, waves, reserves, a speculative-fire burst, an optional late state of 20,000 fallen and 2,000 wrecks, with live frame, heap, GPU and load telemetry. Set ENDURANCE_S for a longer real-time run.

Sight-light fog over the village street (battle-look slice 14): blue's eyes cut by the terrain and the buildings it knows, per pixel; the live frame or a seen/unseen mask; agreement with the simulation's 8 m sweep, the GPU lookup against its oracle vectors, a turned turret and a garrison's eyes.

Model workbench: drop a GLB (or /workbench?bundle=name) to see validator findings and the production render — named views, a 1.8 m figure, the simulation hit box, socket gizmos, clip and phase scrubber, pose inputs, a feed replay through the pose driver, stats, sheets and the impostor bake.

How unseen looks (battle-look slice 15): the fixture's named fog styles over the village street under a 16:00 sun, every number live on sliders with a copyable presentation.fog block; roofs and canopy tops above the eyes; contact glyphs (a hatch plus the red glow, a pale ghost for a last sighting).
